findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator does not support datetime ordering used by audit logs
findings.body: The optimized path uses `OrderedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `self.key` is the `datetime` field. However `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` does `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` on the raw `datetime` object, which raises `TypeError`. Its `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of converting it to a datetime as `DateTimePaginator` does. As a result, any request with `optimized_pagination=true` will 500, making the new pagination path unusable.

findings.title: Negative offset slicing is unsupported by Django QuerySet
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, this code sets `start_offset` to a negative number and executes `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing and raise `TypeError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The comment above says Django handles negative slicing automatically, which is incorrect. A crafted cursor with a negative offset can therefore produce a 500 for users allowed to use the optimized paginator.

findings.title: In-place change from Redis sets to sorted sets breaks existing span buffer keys
findings.body: The span buffer previously stored `span-buf:s:*` keys as Redis sets via `SADD`, `SUNIONSTORE`, and `SSCAN`. This PR changes the same key space to sorted sets using `ZADD` here and `ZSCAN`/`ZUNIONSTORE` later. Existing keys created by the old code are Redis set values and have a TTL of up to `redis_ttl` (default 3600s). During a rolling deploy, new code will issue Z* commands against those set keys and Redis will return WRONGTYPE, causing ingestion/flushing failures and potential span loss until all old keys expire. A migration to a versioned key format, a drain step, or some compatibility handling is needed.

findings.title: Redirect chain resolution limit reduced from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The loop resolving redirects via `HGET` now stops after 1000 iterations instead of 10000. The previous code explicitly noted that deeper segment trees may not be joined correctly when the limit is hit. Lowering the limit makes this failure reachable for traces with parent redirect chains deeper than 1000, causing spans to be associated with the wrong `set_key` and emitted in incorrect segments. If the reduction is intentional for performance or DoS protection, that tradeoff should be documented; otherwise this is a silent data-integrity regression for deep traces.
